children.name: GDP Nowcasting
children.blurb: GDP nowcasting is the practice of estimating current-quarter GDP growth before official statistics are published, using higher-frequency data that arrive during the quarter.

children.name: Synthetic Populations for Policy Analysis
children.blurb: Synthetic populations are artificial datasets of individuals, households, or firms designed to mirror the statistical properties of a real population while containing no actual personal records.

children.blurb: Climate and the economy sits at the intersection of macroeconomic forecasting, environmental accounting, and policy evaluation.

children.name: Agent-Based and Game Theory Models
children.blurb: Agent-based and game theory models in macroeconomic econometrics simulate economies as populations of heterogeneous agents who interact according to strategic rules, rather than as a single representative household or firm.

sections.body: Macroeconomic econometrics is the branch of economics that measures and forecasts economy-wide quantities such as output, inflation, employment, and financial conditions. Artificial intelligence is now used there to process high-frequency and unconventional data, to estimate dynamic models with many parameters, and to extract signals from text. GDP nowcasting systems combine machine learning with mixed-frequency data to produce early estimates before official statistics arrive. Central bank watchers use natural language processing to score policy statements, speeches, and minutes for tone and uncertainty. Synthetic populations let researchers simulate how tax, transfer, or benefit changes might ripple through millions of households. Agent-based and game theory models simulate strategic interactions among firms, banks, households, and governments, and these are working tools in research and policy shops, not just thought experiments.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The field has made real progress on prediction tasks where data are plentiful and the target is stable, such as short-horizon GDP nowcasts and sentiment extraction from central bank text. It has not solved causal inference, long-horizon forecasting, or structural change. Data revisions, regime shifts, and policy breaks can make a model that looked accurate in backtests fail in live use. Central bank communication remains ambiguous by design, so tone scores are useful but not definitive. Synthetic populations depend on calibration and privacy choices, and small errors can compound across many simulated agents. Climate-economy models face deep uncertainty about damages, adaptation, and tipping points, and agent-based models often lack clean external validation, so the honest limit is that AI improves pattern detection and computation but does not remove the need for economic theory, identification, and judgment.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages under this section form a chain from measurement to interpretation to simulation. GDP Nowcasting is the entry point for readers who want to see how mixed-frequency data and machine learning produce early output estimates. Reading Central Bank Communication shows how text models turn policy language into measurable signals for rates, risk, and uncertainty. Synthetic Populations for Policy Analysis moves from aggregate forecasts to distributional questions, letting a reader explore who gains or loses under a policy change. Climate and the Economy connects macroeconomic models to energy, emissions, and physical risk, where the time horizons are long and the uncertainties are large. Agent-Based and Game Theory Models provides the microfoundations for strategic behaviour, including how banks, firms, and households react to one another.
